The total amount charged for all services was nine thousand one hundred forty-nine dollars and fifty cents. Your health insurance paid some of the cost and gave a discount, leaving a balance due of one thousand five hundred sixty-three dollars and thirty-five cents. However, your insurance company letter says you only owe eight hundred eight dollars and eighty-five cents. You should call the billing office to find out why the bill amount does not match your insurance papers.
result.spoken_summary: You have a medical bill from Linnet Valley Medical Center for an emergency room visit. The total charges were over nine thousand dollars. Your insurance paid part of it, but the hospital says you owe one thousand five hundred sixty-three dollars and thirty-five cents. Your insurance statement says you only owe eight hundred eight dollars and eighty-five cents. You should call your insurance company and the hospital billing department to ask why the two amounts are different before you make a payment.
